subject: Request for temporary SLA elevation during launch window
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@cardinalbio.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary SLA uplift for launch period

Hi Connor,

We're launching a major feature on Oct 15 and expect a short, very high burst of traffic (estimated 3–4x our usual RPS for a 72-hour window). Cardinal Bio needs clarity on two things from Redwood before we sign the mutual action plan: 1) whether you can provide a temporary higher-grade SLA for uptime/latency for that 72-hour window, and 2) whether we can get a carve-out from fairness throttling for our top-tier API keys during the window.

Specifically, we'd like to have an elevated p95 latency objective (targeting ~100ms p95) and explicit routing to a reserved pool to avoid noisy-neighbor throttling. We expect to hit ~1.1M tokens/day at peak and will provide a traffic projection.

Attached: launch_traffic_projection.csv; cardinal_sla_request_form.pdf

Can you loop in the account team and ops to confirm feasibility, expected costs, and any preconditions (e.g., warm-up, headers, tokens per-request limits)? If you need an MCA or DocuSign to lock the window, let me know and we'll expedite.

Thanks,
Elaine Park
Senior Platform Engineer | Cardinal Bio
elaine@cardinalbio.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@cardinalbio.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA uplift for launch period

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear runbook and the projection. We're confident we can support a short elevated window, with some operational prerequisites to protect both your traffic and overall cluster fairness. High-level proposal:

- Offer: Temporary "elevated performance window" (configurable, up to 72 hours) with routing to a reserved burst pool and a target p95 latency objective of 120ms for the window.
- Preconditions: 48-hour notice to provision capacity and lock the pool; committed traffic projection (you provided); an agreed Mutual Action Plan (attached draft).
- Fairness and throttling: We will apply per-key priority tagging to reduce fairness rebalanced throttles for your top-tier keys during the window, but full exclusion from fairness is not possible across extreme contention — we can provide explicit carve-outs for reserved pool traffic.
- Testing: We recommend a two-hour canary at 30% traffic before the full window; we'll provide a test checklist and a rollback plan.
- Cost: uplift will be an add-on for reserved capacity + per-token uplift during the window (Laura will send pricing).

I've attached a draft Mutual Action Plan (mutual_action_plan_draft.xlsx) for your review. Laura and Marcus are on this thread to confirm pricing and the technical header/traffic tagging requirements. If that sounds acceptable, please confirm and we'll open the capacity reservation and DocuSign.

Connor O'Brien

Connor — appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple of follow-ups:

- Can you confirm the behavior if we exceed the reserved pool capacity? Will requests be queued, throttled, or routed to a fallback model? We need to define fail-open vs fail-closed.
- On fairness: our legal team wants an assurance that our top-tier API keys will not be subject to tenant-level throttling during the reserved window. You mentioned per-key priority tagging — is that a hard guarantee for the reserved pool?
- For costs, please send an estimate ASAP. We need to lock budget this week.

We can sign the M.A.P. once we have the cost and the operational acceptance criteria written down.

Elaine — quick pricing and guarantees from our side: 

- Pricing: one-time reserved-window fee: $5,000 for up to 72 hours (covers dedicated burst pool reservation + pre-warm). Token overage during window billed at $0.0025 per token above baseline.
- Fairness guarantee: Reserved pool traffic will be isolated from standard tenant fairness controls. Requests that are routed to the reserved pool will not be throttled by fairness policies. If your traffic exceeds reserved pool capacity, excess requests will be routed to a best-effort fallback (subject to standard quotas) unless you opt into the overflow route to a lower-cost model.
- SLA credits: If average p95 across the window exceeds the agreed objective by >20% due to our provisioning error, we'll issue a pro-rated account credit. Specific credit terms to be included in the M.A.P.

Next steps: confirm the window dates, sign the M.A.P., and Marcus will queue the capacity reservation and provide the header spec for priority tagging. Attached pricing_summary.pdf.

Laura Bennett

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-02T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA uplift for launch period

Elaine — technical notes for the reservation and client changes: 

- Priority header: include header 'X-RDWD-Priority: cardinal-launch' on all requests you want routed to the reserved pool. We'll map that header to your API keys server-side.
- Warm-up: reserved pools will need ~20–30 minutes of synthetic traffic to warm KV caches; plan for a 2-hour canary at 30% traffic as Connor suggested.
- Overflow behavior: by default overflow goes to a best-effort queue that may experience standard fairness throttling; we can configure overflow to route to a smaller, cheaper model instance (lossy) if you prefer predictable degraded responses rather than throttled errors.
- Acceptance tests: we'll run a quick p95 latency sweep and token throughput validation during the canary. If you accept, we'll attach these acceptance criteria to the M.A.P.

I'll open the capacity reservation ticket once you confirm dates.

—Marcus
